scenes.title: Key ideas
items: Public data APIs (e.g. protocol analytics sites, explorers) return TVL, fees, yields and…
Scripts that only read (never hold keys) can check health factors, pegs and utilisation,…
scenes.vo: First, Reading without code: block explorers' Read tabs show a contract's public state (for example a lending market's parameters, your position). Next, Public data APIs (for example protocol analytics sites, explorers) return T.V.L., fees, yields and prices as JSON. Then, R.P.C.: a node endpoint that lets a script read chain state directly (balances, contract calls). Use a reputable provider; reading is free or cheap. Also, Scripts that only read (never hold keys) can check health factors, pegs and utilisation, and send you alerts. And finally, Rule: tools that read are low-risk; tools that sign follow Lesson 14.2 (scoped, capped, revocable permissions). Never put a seed phrase or private key in a script, a file or an environment variable on a shared machine.

And finally, Rule: tools that read are low-risk; tools that sign follow Lesson 14.2 (scoped, capped, revocable permissions). Never put a seed phrase or private key in a script, a file or an environment variable on a shared machine.
